Setup guide for the PC. Waking needs the settings in section 1. Remote shutdown over SSH (section 2) is optional.
A magic packet wakes a PC that is off or asleep, but only if its network card still has power and is listening. Use a network cable: Wi-Fi rarely works for wake-up.

In the BIOS/UEFI, turn on Wake on LAN (names vary: Wake on LAN, Power On By PCI-E, Resume by PCI-E). If there is an ErP, EuP or deep-sleep option, turn it off, because it cuts power to the network card.
Find the network interface name (for example enp8s0):
Check the Wake-on setting. It must show g:
Turn it on (this resets at reboot):
To keep it after reboots with NetworkManager (replace the connection name, see nmcli connection show):
Open Device Manager, double-click your network adapter, tab Power Management: tick \u201cAllow this device to wake the computer\u201d and \u201cOnly allow a magic packet to wake the computer\u201d.
Same window, tab Advanced: set \u201cWake on Magic Packet\u201d to Enabled (if it is listed).

Turn off Fast Startup: Control Panel \u2192 Power Options \u2192 Choose what the power buttons do \u2192 Change settings that are currently unavailable \u2192 untick \u201cTurn on fast startup\u201d. With Fast Startup on, a PC that was shut down often ignores the magic packet.
In WakeDeck, add the device with the PC\u2019s MAC address. Find it here:
Broadcast address: the last address of your network, for example 192.168.1.255 for 192.168.1.x (the default 255.255.255.255 also works on the same network). Port: 9.
The app logs in with its own key, never a password. The PC needs an SSH server, and the app\u2019s public key must be added to it. The commands below already contain your key.

If it still refuses: check that the firewall allows TCP port 22 (the OpenSSH feature normally adds the rule), and that the account is not a Microsoft Entra ID account, which cannot use keys.

In the device\u2019s edit screen fill in the host (IP or name), the SSH user (your PC account name) and the port (22). Tap Shut down now. The first time, check that the fingerprint shown matches the PC\u2019s, then tap Trust. The PC\u2019s fingerprint:

\u201cThe PC refused the SSH key\u201d: wrong key or user name. \u201cCould not connect\u201d: the PC is off, or the host, port or firewall is wrong. \u201cThe PC replied with an error\u201d: on Linux usually the sudoers rule. \u201cThe PC\u2019s SSH key changed\u201d: the PC was reinstalled or its SSH keys were regenerated; trust the new key only if you expect that.

From outside your home network you first need a way into it, for example a WireGuard or Tailscale VPN. A magic packet is a broadcast, and many VPNs do not forward broadcasts. Put your network\u2019s broadcast address (for example 192.168.1.255) in the device. If waking still does not work remotely, a small always-on device at home that sends the packet for you (a router with Wake-on-LAN, or a Raspberry Pi) is the usual solution. Remote shutdown over SSH works over a VPN as long as the PC\u2019s address is reachable.

The message after tapping a launcher shortcut needs notifications allowed for WakeDeck (Settings \u2192 Apps \u2192 WakeDeck \u2192 Notifications). Without it MagicOS hides the message, but the wake still works.

Widgets refresh the status in the background and MagicOS may stop that to save battery. Allow WakeDeck to run in the background (Settings \u2192 Battery, exclude WakeDeck from battery optimization). The refresh button on a widget always works.

Remote problems: \u201cno network or VPN connection\u201d means the phone has no route to that address, so connect the VPN first. \u201cBroadcast address not found\u201d means the name or address in the device cannot be resolved. A VPN may also accept the packet but never deliver it: the app cannot tell, because a magic packet has no reply. Check that the PC turns on, and look at its status in the list.
How to set this up on the PC
Tap a group to choose its devices.

Open System Settings \u2192 Battery (MacBook) or Energy (desktop Mac) \u2192 Options, and turn on \u201cWake for network access\u201d. Waking works best over Ethernet: on a MacBook use a USB-C or Thunderbolt Ethernet adapter, and keep it plugged into power. A sleeping Mac on Wi-Fi often ignores the magic packet.

On Wi-Fi, also turn off \u201cPrivate Wi-Fi address\u201d for your network (System Settings \u2192 Wi-Fi \u2192 Details), or the Mac gets a different MAC address. In the list below, \u201cEthernet Address\u201d is the MAC address of each port.
Turn on the SSH server: System Settings \u2192 General \u2192 Sharing \u2192 Remote Login, and allow your user.
